metadata.title: DINOv2: Learning Robust Visual Features without Supervision

problem.value: Text-guided pretraining limits the information retained about images because captions only approximate rich visual content.

evidence.quote: This form of text-guided pretraining limits the information that can be retained about the image since captions only approximate the rich information in images, and complex pixel-level information may not surface with this supervision.

problem.value: Scaling self-supervised learning on uncurated datasets typically leads to a significant drop in feature quality due to a lack of data control.

evidence.quote: Some efforts on scaling these approaches beyond ImageNet-1k have been attempted (Caron et al., 2019;Goyal et al., 2021;2022a), but they focused on uncurated datasets, which typically lead to a significant drop in the quality of the features.

contributions.value: An automatic pipeline to build a dedicated, diverse, and curated image dataset from uncurated sources.

evidence.quote: In terms of data, we propose an automatic pipeline to build a dedicated, diverse, and curated image dataset instead of uncurated data, as typically done in the self-supervised literature.

contributions.value: Training a 1B parameter ViT model and distilling it into smaller models that surpass existing general-purpose features on most benchmarks.

evidence.quote: In terms of models, we train a ViT model (Dosovitskiy et al., 2021) with 1B parameters and distill it into a series of smaller models that surpass the best available general-purpose features, OpenCLIP (Ilharco et al., 2021) on most of the benchmarks at image and pixel levels.

contributions.value: Technical improvements that accelerate and stabilize training at scale, making the approach faster and more memory efficient.

evidence.quote: Most of the technical contributions aim at accelerating and stabilizing the training at scale.

method_summary.value: An image-level cross-entropy loss objective between student and teacher network class tokens extracted from different crops.

evidence.quote: We consider the cross-entropy loss between the features extracted from a student and a teacher network.

method_summary.value: A patch-level objective utilizing masked input patches for the student network and visible patches for the teacher network.

evidence.quote: We randomly mask some of the input patches given to the student, but not to the teacher.

method_summary.value: Sinkhorn-Knopp centering is used for the teacher network instead of standard softmax-centering.

evidence.quote: Ruan et al. (2023) recommend to replace the teacher softmax-centering step of DINO and iBot by the Sinkhorn-Knopp (SK) batch normalization of SwAV (Caron et al., 2020).

method_summary.value: The KoLeo regularizer is applied to encourage a uniform span of the features within a batch.

evidence.quote: The KoLeo regularizer derives from the Kozachenko-Leonenko differential entropy estimator (see Beirlant et al. (1997); Delattre & Fournier (2017)) and encourages a uniform span of the features within a batch.

method_summary.value: The image resolution is increased during a short period at the end of pretraining.

evidence.quote: However, training at high resolution is time and memory demanding, and instead, we increase the resolution of images to 518 × 518 during a short period at the end of pretraining.

novelty.value: Unlike prior work that shares parameters between DINO and iBOT projection heads, separate heads are used at scale.

evidence.quote: At scale, we observed that the opposite is true, and we therefore use two separate heads in all our experiments.

compute.value: Compute cluster for LVD-142M dataset creation

evidence.quote: The whole processing is distributed on a compute cluster of 20 nodes equipped with 8 V100-32GB GPUs and takes less than two days to produce the LVD-142M dataset.
We train models on A100 GPUs using PyTorch 2.0.

future_work.value: Continue scaling models and data along the same axes.

evidence.quote: We expect that more of these properties will emerge at larger scales of models and data, akin to instruction emergence in large language models, and plan to continue scaling along these axes.

future_work.value: Leverage linear layer compatibility to train a language-enabled AI system that processes visual features.

evidence.quote: In future work, we plan to leverage this ability to train a a language-enabled AI system that can process visual features as if they were word tokens, and extract the required information to ground the system.

claims.value: The proposed technical improvements make the approach roughly 2 times faster and require 3 times less memory than similar discriminative self-supervised methods.

evidence.quote: These improvements make our approach around 2× faster and require 3× less memory than similar discriminative self-supervised methods, allowing us to leverage longer training with larger batch sizes.

claims.value: Self-supervised pretraining alone is a viable approach for learning transferable frozen features comparable to top openly available weakly-supervised models.

evidence.quote: We conclude that selfsupervised pretraining alone is a good candidate for learning transferable frozen features that are competitive with the best openly available weakly-supervised models.
